description:
Our Project Vision
We are building an advanced decision-support tool to help farmers adapt to shifting climates using NASA Earth observations.
summary:
Yieldary AI, a precision agriculture and farm-adaptation platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). Using a Django and React/TypeScript stack integrated with Google Earth Engine, Yieldary AI transforms orbital datasets—including SMAP L4, GPM IMERG, MODIS, Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, SRTM 90m, GEDI LiDAR, and NASA POWER—into actionable farm intelligence without requiring on-farm IoT hardware.

The platform addresses the challenge through three core modules: Space-to-Soil Telemetry (tracking soil moisture, water stress, VPD, and vegetation vigor), Terrain & Erosion Analysis (computing a LiDAR-adjusted RUSLE topsoil erosion score), and a Gemini-powered Crop Rotation & Climate What-If Engine with deterministic fallbacks. It also includes a 3-season rotation simulator, leaf/soil diagnostics, subsidy matching, and a multilingual voice helpdesk in English, Malayalam, Tamil, and Hindi.

This is important for smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable regions like Kerala, helping them prevent topsoil loss, adapt to erratic rainfall, and protect yields and livelihoods.
details:
Yieldary AI is a precision agriculture and farm-adaptation platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data"). It translates raw orbital Earth observation data into localized crop rotation strategies, erosion risk assessments, and cluster-level farm management.

5-Step Operational Pipeline

  1. Farmer Onboarding & Geolocation: Farmers search their village via OpenStreetMap Nominatim to capture exact GPS coordinates, verify their email with a 6-digit OTP, and register securely (Argon2 password hashing + SimpleJWT). Registration triggers a background thread that precomputes satellite reports for their plot.
  2. Module 1 — Space-to-Soil Telemetry: Queries Google Earth Engine (GEE) and NASA POWER in a batched server call to compute monthly soil moisture (SMAP L4), rainfall (GPM IMERG), evapotranspiration (MODIS MOD16A2GF), Water Stress Index (WSI), vegetative vigor (Sentinel-2 & Landsat 8/9 NDVI, EVI, NDWI), Vapor Pressure Deficit (GLDAS-2.1 VPD), and Frost Risk.
  3. Module 2 — Terrain, Canopy & Soil Erosion Analysis: Combines NASA/CGIAR SRTM 90m slope, GPM wettest-month rainfall intensity, OpenLandMap USDA soil texture, ESA WorldCover 10m land cover, and NASA GEDI ISS LiDAR canopy height (rh98) to compute an adjusted RUSLE Topsoil Erosion Risk Score (0–100).
  4. Module 3 — Crop Rotation & Climate What-If Engine: Feeds telemetry, erosion metrics, 3-year ERA5/MODIS history, farmer constraint sliders (water, budget, market demand, equipment), and climate perturbations ($\pm 50\%$ rainfall, $+0\text{–}4^\circ\text{C}$ temperature) into Google Gemini (gemini-2.0-flash $\rightarrow$ gemini-2.5-flash-lite $\rightarrow$ gemini-2.5-flash) with a strict Pydantic schema (RotationResponseSchema). It outputs 3 strategies—Baseline, Soil-Resilience Intercrop, and Low-ET Water-Saver—in English, Malayalam, Tamil, or Hindi. If the LLM is unreachable or quota-limited, a deterministic _fallback_decision_matrix() computes all scores and translations locally so the endpoint always returns HTTP 200 OK.
  5. Precision Agriculture Suite: Adds 6 integrated operational tools in the same Yieldary AI dashboard: a Cluster Command Heatmap & One-Tap Satellite Field Profiler, a 3-Season Kharif-Rabi-Zaid Pareto Simulator, an AI Visual Leaf & Soil Card Scanner, an AI4Bharat Multilingual Voice Helpdesk, a Cadastral Farmer CRM, and a Government Subsidy Scheme Match Wizard.

Core Technical Innovations

  • Multi-Sensor Orbital Fusion for Erosion Modeling: Instead of relying on static slope maps alone, Module 2 fuses SRTM 90m topography, GPM rainfall erosivity, ESA WorldCover bare-ground ratios, and NASA GEDI 98th-percentile LiDAR canopy height into a dynamic RUSLE proxy.
  • Interactive "What-If" Climate & Economic Sandbox: Farmers can stress-test crop rotations in real time against hypothetical rainfall shifts, temperature spikes, and personal capital/equipment constraints, or optimize 3-season Kharif-Rabi-Zaid sequences via a multi-objective Pareto fitness equation.
  • Hybrid Generative + Deterministic AI: Pairing structured Gemini JSON outputs with a mathematically grounded _fallback_decision_matrix() combines natural-language regional agronomy with guaranteed numerical reliability.
  • Unified Mission Control & Precision Ag Suite: Seamlessly connects individual farm telemetry, leaf/soil card computer vision, multilingual voice synthesis, and government scheme matching inside a single bento-grid interface.

Benefits

  • Zero-Hardware Sensing: Delivers root-zone soil moisture, canopy height, slope, and microclimate telemetry using orbital satellites rather than expensive on-farm IoT sensors.
  • Proactive Disease & Climate Resilience: Detects 48-hour Fungal Blast Epidemic windows ($\text{RH} \ge 85\%$ and $22.0^\circ\text{C} \le T \le 28.5^\circ\text{C}$) and stomatal closure stress ($\text{VPD} > 1.6\text{ kPa}$) before crop damage escalates, enabling SMS/IVR broadcasts to 1,280+ farmers.
  • Actionable, Non-Technical Decisions: Converts complex biophysical indices into clear 0–100 suitability scores, visual gauges, and native-language advisories with read-aloud audio.
  • 100% Uptime Guarantee: Deterministic mathematical fallbacks (for both the Gemini rotation advisor and the Scikit-Learn Random Forest / Gaussian Mahalanobis 22-crop classifier) ensure farmers never face broken screens during API outages.

Impact of the Project

The project aims to bridge the gap between complex NASA/ESA Earth observation datasets and everyday decision-making for smallholder farmers and agricultural clusters—especially in climate-vulnerable, steep-terrain regions such as Kerala (e.g., Idukki). By helping farmers anticipate water deficits, prevent monsoon-driven topsoil erosion, disrupt pest cycles through 3-season crop rotation, and match directly with Central and State government subsidies, Yieldary AI seeks to protect soil health, stabilize yields, and improve farm profitability under shifting climate conditions.

Factors Considered

  • Regional & Tropical Accuracy: Standard NDVI saturates in dense tropical plantations (such as Idukki), so the team included EVI to correct for aerosols and dense canopy, alongside GLDAS psychrometrics to catch fungal blast incubation windows.
  • Accessibility & Language Inclusion: Recognizing that smallholder farmers may not read English or complex charts, the team built native Malayalam, Tamil, Hindi, and English support, Web Speech API read-aloud, and a 16kHz WAV voice helpdesk.
  • Fault Tolerance & Latency: To prevent slow satellite queries or API rate limits from blocking users, the team implemented async post-signup precomputation, single-call .getInfo() GEE batching, and deterministic local fallbacks.
  • Data Security & Practical Viability: Protected user accounts with Argon2 hashing, OTP verification, and JWT bearer tokens, while grounding crop recommendations in real-world constraints (water availability, capital budget, labor, equipment, and subsidy eligibility).

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Development Environment & AI Coding Tools: Antigravity, Visual Studio Code (VS Code), and Google Gemini for architecture, code generation, and debugging.
  • Backend & Database: Python, Django, Django REST Framework, SimpleJWT, Argon2 (Argon2PasswordHasher), Pydantic, and SQLite (db.sqlite3).
  • Frontend & Visualization: TypeScript, React, Vite, Axios, custom SVG Cubic Bezier charts and radial gauges, OpenStreetMap terrain/heatmap layers, and the Web Speech API.
  • Geospatial & Climate APIs: Google Earth Engine (GEE), NASA POWER API, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and orbital datasets including Copernicus Sentinel-2, NASA/USGS Landsat 8 & 9, NASA MODIS (NDVI, ET, Land Cover), NASA SMAP L4, NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG, ECMWF ERA5-Land, NASA GLDAS-2.1, NASA/CGIAR SRTM 90m, OpenLandMap, ESA WorldCover 10m, and NASA GEDI LiDAR.
  • AI, ML & Speech Engines: Google Gemini GenAI (google-genai), Scikit-Learn Random Forest + Gaussian Mahalanobis classifier (trained on 2,200 records across 22 crop classes), LLaVA multi-modal vision diagnostics, AI4Bharat Indic ASR/IndicTrans2, and a custom 16kHz 16-bit mono PCM WAV synthesizer.
  • Hardware: Standard developer workstations for building and hosting, paired with spaceborne Earth observation satellites and ISS LiDAR (GEDI) as the remote-sensing layer.
